name: 浅草 更科天狐（さらしな てんこ） (Asakusa Sarashina Tenko)

claims.text: No source found addresses shared-kitchen or cross-contamination handling for celiac-level safety; the restaurant's claims are about ingredient composition (no wheat binder, reformulated tsuyu) rather than facility-level gluten controls.

FindMeGlutenFree notes this establishment is NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility and may not be safe for those with celiac disease, and recommends contacting the establishment directly about safety precautions.
Described as '99% gluten free'; gluten-containing items are marked on the menu with a 🌾 emoji — i.e., wheat is present on premises, contradicting an all-GF framing.
Japanese-language coverage/summary states '一部のメニューには小麦が含まれる場合がある' (some menu items may contain wheat).

One reviewer noted that although told everything was gluten-free, English communication was difficult and the menu had no clear labelling, recommending a Japanese Celiac Pass for very sensitive diners.
Restaurant serves gluten-free shrimp tempura (a fried item); no source confirms a dedicated fryer or cross-contact protocol for fried items.
The Edo-style dipping sauce is made from bonito essence, and the menu includes duck-broth dishes and chicken — confirming fish/animal-based dashi and no vegan preparation.

The restaurant states it developed a proprietary 'Edo tsuyu' specifically to eliminate the wheat-derived gluten that a normal soba dipping sauce picks up from its soy sauce, applying this across all three noodle varieties.

All three house soba noodles (juwari, sarashina, kurobiki) are 100% buckwheat with no wheat binder added, using flour from Miyamoto Seifun, the long-established Nerima mill that also supplies the noted Kanda Yabu Soba.
The dipping sauce (tsuyu) itself was reformulated by the kitchen to remove wheat gluten, rather than just serving gluten-free noodles alongside a conventional sauce.

name: 浅草豆花大王 (Asakusa Tofa King (Asakusa Toka Daiō))

claims.text: The shop also serves congyoubing (a wheat-flour Taiwanese scallion pancake) alongside the soy-based douhua, indicating the kitchen is not exclusively wheat-free even though the douhua itself contains no wheat.
A search-engine summary of the shop's Vegewel restaurant listing indicates that aside from the condensed milk (練乳) used on one shaved-ice item, the shop's sweets use no animal-derived ingredients.
Search-engine summaries citing the shop's Vegewel listing describe it as animal-product-free aside from the condensed milk on shaved ice, and note the shop welcomes vegan customers.

name: コンテナ（CONTAINER Cafe&Bar） (CONTAINER (Container Cafe & Bar))

claims.text: The lunch menu includes lighter items like risotto, croque monsieur, and salads, while dinner features high-protein, low-sugar dishes — croque monsieur is a wheat-bread sandwich, confirming active wheat/flour handling in the same kitchen that makes the GF cakes.
claims.source: https://san-tatsu.jp/articles/183522/ (via search summary of the article's menu description)

claims.text: GF claims across all sources are scoped specifically to cakes ('All cakes are gluten-free, made with mineral-rich brown sugar'); no source states the savory food, bar items, or sauces are gluten-free, and none mentions any cross-contamination control or dedicated kitchen.

CONTAINER Cafe&Bar does not appear in FindMeGlutenFree's Shinjuku City or Shinjuku 'Most Celiac Friendly' listings — no celiac/coeliac diner reviews exist to corroborate real cross-contamination safety.
All cakes on the menu are made gluten-free using kibi (unrefined cane) sugar rather than white sugar; for specific allergy needs beyond gluten, callers are directed to confirm ingredients by phone.
Every cake on the menu is gluten-free, lightly sweetened with mineral-rich kibi sugar.
Organic coffee and tea are used, including a 97%-decaffeinated coffee option and 100% fruit juices/organic cordial sodas for those avoiding caffeine or seeking lighter drink options.

name: D.I.Y. salad & delicatessen（ディーアイワイ サラダ アンド デリカテッセン） (D.I.Y. Salad & Delicatessen)

claims.text: No source describes a dedicated gluten-free prep area; the counter also prepares meat and other deli items alongside salads, so cross-contact for gluten and other allergens has not been independently confirmed.
Store listings note the shop accommodates vegan diners and allergy-related requests alongside its gluten-free-friendly, additive-free positioning, but do not describe a formal allergy protocol.
Marketed as offering gluten-free, refined-sugar-free and additive-free food and drink options for health-conscious customers.
The build-your-own ('D.I.Y.') format lets diners choose every topping and dressing themselves, making it easier to avoid specific ingredients compared to a fixed-menu restaurant.

name: ドーター ブティック トーキョー (Daughter Boutique Tokyo)

claims.text: Operates as a dedicated plant-based, gluten-free workshop — only gluten-free and plant-based ingredients are used in production, so the company states there is no cross-contamination concern.

The FindMeGlutenFree celiac review that surfaced under Daughter Boutique searches actually describes a different, explicitly non-dedicated restaurant: 'even though they are not dedicated for Gluten Free they have many GF option menu and as the owners daughter is gluten free also.' It is a mismatch and provides NO celiac-grade corroboration for Daughter Boutique.

Japanese consumer-affairs guidance warns that rice-flour (米粉) products may contain wheat-derived ingredients and that allergy accidents have occurred; combined with no mandatory Japanese cross-contamination labeling, an all-GF bakery's 'no cross-contamination' claim is not self-verifying without third-party non-gluten (<20ppm) testing.

Independent write-ups indicate the brand currently operates largely as an online shop / OEM / wholesale workshop with no vetted dine-in retail presence, limiting independent celiac on-site verification.
As a fully plant-based bakery, no animal-derived ingredients (dairy, egg, honey) are used anywhere in the kitchen.
For in-person pickup, customers are advised to reserve items by phone or email at least a few days in advance rather than simply walking in.

Every item is made without wheat, dairy, or egg, using natural sweeteners like beet sugar and maple syrup instead of refined white sugar or artificial sweeteners, and without chemical synthetic additives.

name: グリーン イタリアン トルチャ (Green Italian TORCIA)

claims.text: Listed on Vegewel's restaurant guide as offering a gluten-free menu option, and reviewers note being glad a gluten-free menu is available.
All vegan dishes are made without meat, egg, dairy, or refined white sugar, and are clearly marked 'Vegan' on the menu, so vegan diners can identify safe dishes easily.
The restaurant is designed so vegan and non-vegan diners can eat together, each ordering from the appropriate part of the menu, which reviewers highlight as useful for mixed dietary groups.

name: HealthyTOKYO CBD ショップ&カフェ 新宿マルイ本館 (HealthyTOKYO CBD Shop & Cafe Shinjuku Marui )

claims.text: HealthyTOKYO is not a dedicated gluten-free facility and may not be safe for those with celiac disease, with the establishment recommending people contact them directly to inquire about safety precautions.

Items are labeled as gluten free on the menu, and while they have some regular sandwiches available, the lasagnas are covered so cross contamination would be minimal — confirming gluten-containing items are prepared in the same cafe alongside GF items.
Establishment described as NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility; customers advised to contact directly about cross-contamination protocols and food preparation procedures.
Marketing/reviews confirm 'most' Shinjuku menu items are gluten-free (not all), e.g. the CBD Mont Blanc is GF and vegan — implying non-GF items also on offer.
店舗の全ての食品・ドリンクメニューが100%ヴィーガン（動物性食品不使用）で提供されている。
CBDクッキーやケーキ類は小麦粉の代わりに米粉を使用するなど、ほとんどのメニューがグルテンフリーで作られている。

name: Be green by KIELO COFFEE (ビー グリーン バイ キエロ コーヒー)

claims.text: The full sweets/bakery menu is gluten-free with no wheat baked goods found on the menu, so there is no wheat flour handled at the pastry counter; still a small shared café/roastery with no published allergen protocol, so cross-contact cannot be certified.

The establishment is NOT a dedicated gluten-free facility and may not be safe for those with celiac disease. Please contact the establishment directly to inquire about safety precautions. Despite offering gluten-free options, the establishment is reported not to have a specific gluten-free menu.

Original 'KIELO COFFEE' (Taito/Akihabara) is a specialty-coffee café serving only some vegan/GF sweets in a mixed kitchen — distinct from the all-GF Hongo 'Be green' location, creating brand-name confusion that can route a celiac to an unsafe kitchen.

No allergen or celiac cross-contact protocol is published on the shop's own channels (afterthree.jp/begreen, stores.jp site, Instagram); GF/vegan claims come only from lifestyle/vegan directories and blogs.
No soy sauce / savoury cooking involved — menu is coffee, plant-milk drinks and gluten-free sweets only, so wheat-in-soy-sauce is not a concern here.
Fully plant-based operation: all milks are oat/almond/soy/pistachio and all desserts are vegan, so no dairy or egg is used on premises.
Store philosophy emphasises direct conversation with customers; no formal written allergy protocol was published, so verify wheat/cross-contact verbally on arrival.
「ドリンクやデザートはすべて植物性の材料で作られており ヴィーガンかつグルテンフリー」 — all drinks and desserts are plant-based, vegan and gluten-free.
「スイーツメニューもすべてヴィーガンかつグルテンフリー」 — the entire sweets menu is vegan and gluten-free; signature carrot cake is rice-flour (米粉) based.
Vegewel lists the shop as vegan-certified with a gluten-free menu.
